PMOE-TX-H-006.q: Across two consistently measured periods, foreign purchases of domestic bonds rise while domestic purchases of foreign assets are unchanged. Which accounting change follows, without identifying how quickly trade adjusts?

NCO falls, while NX must rise
NCO rises, and NX must be higher

PMOE-RER-M-004.q: Let e be foreign currency per domestic currency and ε = eP/P*. The domestic currency depreciates nominally while domestic prices grow more slowly than foreign prices. What happens to ε?

It stays fixed because the two changes offset
It rises because lower domestic inflation raises P/P*
Its direction is ambiguous because both nominal and real rates change

PMOE-RER-M-004.reason: Actual sign defect: nominal depreciation and lower relative domestic inflation reinforce; they do not offset.

PMOE-RER-M-001.q: A domestic basket costs 120 domestic currency units; a comparable foreign basket costs 150 foreign currency units. With e = 2 foreign currency units per domestic unit and ε = eP/P*, what is ε?

1.25 foreign baskets per domestic basket
0.625 foreign basket per domestic basket
2.50 foreign baskets per domestic basket

PMOE-RER-B2-001.q: A basket costs P = 160 domestic currency units and its foreign counterpart costs P* = 100 foreign units. At e = 0.5 foreign currency unit per domestic unit, what is ε = eP/P*?
PMOE-RER-B2-001.feedback: The domestic basket costs 0.5 × 160 = 80 foreign currency units. Dividing by 100 foreign currency units per foreign basket gives ε = 0.80 foreign basket per domestic basket.
PMOE-RER-B2-001.reason: Standalone formula inputs omit quote orientation and price units.

PMOE-FX-R-001.q: In the NCO-based FX model, NCO is fixed. A student says a higher exchange rate must increase the quantity supplied. Which correction distinguishes a movement along vertical supply from a shift?

PMOE-POL-H-002.q: A tariff is imposed while national saving and domestic investment remain unchanged. What is the general-equilibrium NX result in the textbook model?
